findings.summary: The two garment sprites lost the outline that names them, which is worse than the published version. The sweater is a bell-shaped trapezoid: its sleeves hang down along the body and show only as small cuffs at the hem, so at 1x it reads as a dress or a sack. The detail page makes this plainer at full size. The coat is two upright slabs with short cuff stubs at the bottom and reads as a vest or a pair of columns. In the published version (1.2.0-rc.9 s2) and in rc.1, both garments had sleeves leaving the shoulders at an angle and read at once. The step-1 wording technically allows what was drawn: an arm that runs down beside the body and flares 1 unit at the cuff meets 'angles away, 1 unit out every 1–3 rows, far end 2+ units from the centre line'. Only the subjective name test (step 5) could catch it, and it has no concrete criterion. The tee, which has room for its sleeves, kept them spread.
findings.promptFix: Draw every item in the view that shows its defining parts apart from the body: front-on, laid out, with limbs, handles, sleeves, spouts or straps extended outward where the real object lets them. A part must never be tucked, folded or hanging against the body. Each defining part attached to the body has its far end at least 3 units outside the body's own width, and you can see where it joins the body in the top half of its length, not only at the hem or base. Name test, concretely: cover every inner detail and colour and ask whether the outline alone still shows each defining part as a separate lobe. If a defining part does not stick out of the body's outline, redraw it extended.

findings.summary: The towels sprite is a box with a loop on top and a folded edge. In the same grid it reads as a shopping bag and sits close to the tote (box plus top handle), against the set-mates step that applies to items in one grid.

The blog hero's only action ('Read the featured post') is an outlined secondary button. The page's gold commit is the footer Subscribe. The reference hero carries its gold primary inside the hero window, so the first screen here has no strong call to action.

notes: SCOPE: screen step, 1 sample of each app (20261019-020124). Every gate passes (eval-1.md). Palette consistency 0.938, type consistency 1, reference spacing overlap 0.888. Smoke tests are not run at this step. The harness measured no layout defects, so there was nothing to confirm or dismiss. Known capture gap, not penalized: the settings plan-dialog scrim ends at about 900px in the full-page capture. Light and dark captures are identical because the system is dark only.

REGRESSION CHECK vs critic-1 on 1.3.0-rc.1: its one major (item sprites well under half their window) is FIXED. All 11 grid sprites are 21 visible units, and their ink spans about 41–42% of the window at 1440px (home-desktop-dark.png). On the detail pages the ink is about 47% (the tote and sweater detail screenshots). The tall backpack and tote are now as wide as the rest. The rc.1 minors are not re-raised. Several are still visible: the skillet reads as a magnifier, the blog newsletter h2 has no dithered rule, the blog ground sprites are small, the settings and dashboard sidebars stop above the ground strip, and the store container is wider than the blog's. The dashboard sidebar now uses bullets like settings.

UPDATE GOAL (generalization, 1.3.0 plus the rc.2 size fix): REACHED for size and for the generalization items this sample can show. Result counts are plain captions ('Showing 11 products', 'Showing 6 of 6 posts', 'Showing 8 of 8 projects'). Block meters appear only against real maximums: uptime, the bio character limit (42/160) and the free-shipping threshold in the cart. Each kind of screen has its own scene: a catalogue strip, a detail Banner shared across products with the sign word varied by category (BAGS, WEAR), a cart strip, and a shared article Banner. The chart and activity panels end level. KPI tiles are one row. NOT REACHED in one respect, which is the major: the garment silhouettes regressed against published, and the generalized step-1 wording permits it.

Two-column product detail: the picture column ends about 200px above the purchase column in the full-page capture, but .detail-media is position:sticky under the header, which the spec's two-column rule allows. Not a finding.

SIGNATURE (3): present in all four apps and placed as Applying the concept says. That means the full-bleed blog hero with a dithered halo moon (drawings/home-d1.png vs reference p1-i1.png), banners and strips per kind of screen, an inline article figure, framed vignettes in empty states (dashboard state-empty-filter, commerce cart), the checkered ground strip on every route, the gold ▶ marker and hue top bars. Motion is stepped: nc-drift runs 120000ms with steps(120) on the product banner (motion-products-merino-crew-sweater-m1.png). Marked down for the garment regression.

OTHER SCORES. Fidelity (4): night ground, cream pixel type, 4px windows, dithered rules under h2s, hard-shadow gold commits and hue bars, as in reference p1-desktop-light.png, without copying its cabin, figure or snow. Hierarchy (4): scene and h1 first, then 48px KPIs and prices. States (4): the first invalid field gets a gold focus frame and the rest danger frames with '!' messages (settings state-profile-errors). Card hover shows the ▶ marker on a lighter card. The plan dialog is a titled window with Cancel and a gold Confirm. Empty filter results show a vignette and a framed ▶ Clear filters. Spacing (4) and polish (4): controls sharing a row share one height, radius 0, no browser defaults left over.
VERDICT INPUT: no blocker. One major, the garment silhouette regression. It is spec-caused, and with one sample it gates this screen. Two minors are listed once.
